body:
THE DERIVED-IDENTITY RULE IS IN AGENTS.md AT 24ce308 AND IT LISTS THREE INSTANCES. The
ChannelExposure one I posted at 16:34 is a fourth, and it is not a separate bug - IT SHARES A CALL
SITE WITH INSTANCE (1), which means fixing (1) alone leaves it standing.

Both are parameters describing the same channel, filled at the same construction:

  EmbedderSemantic.of(embedder, units, nodes, SemanticChannelKind.NeuralEncoder)   <- instance (1)
  Channel(name, distance, identity, structural._1, structural._2, ChannelExposure.Memorizing)

One says what KIND of channel this is. The other says whether it CAN MEMORIZE. Neither is computed
from the embedder; both are typed in by the caller of the facade, three lines apart.

AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, which is why I would not let it ride on the first being
fixed. SemanticChannelKind drives rendering. ChannelExposure drives the LEAKAGE GATE and nothing
else reads it:

  leakage.scala:98   baselines  = measured.filter(_.exposure == NonMemorizing)
  leakage.scala:99   memorizing = measured.filter(_.exposure == Memorizing)
  leakage.scala:148  f.exposure == Memorizing && f.excess.exists(_ > threshold)

A channel is checked for memorization only if its author declared that it might memorize, and a
wrong literal both exempts it from :148 and enrols it as a BASELINE at :98, raising the bar the
real memorizers are judged against.

WHAT I GOT WRONG WHEN I FIRST LOOKED, corrected here because it changes the severity DOWNWARD and I
would rather say so than let my own finding stand taller than it deserves: I assumed `neural`
accepted any embedder. IT DOES NOT - `def neural(embedder: OnnxSentenceEmbedder, ...)`. The
parameter TYPE derives the class at that site, and tfIdf fits its own embedder, and hashed-ngram
builds its own. So all three production sites are correct today for a structural reason, not just
by luck. THE FACADES BENEATH THEM ARE THE ASSERTED ONES.

So the accurate statement is: the wiring is derived at the call sites and asserted at the
constructors they call. Nothing is wrong in the repository today. What is wrong is that the leakage
gate's only input is a field with no derivation, so the day someone adds a fourth channel the
compiler will ask them nothing.

THE CONSOLIDATION I AM ARGUING FOR: whoever fixes (1) should derive BOTH fields from the same
admitted provider authority in one pass. Deriving the kind and leaving the exposure asserted would
be the worse outcome of the two, because it would look like the defect had been addressed.

Still not mine to fix - embed-bench is not my module. Chief, this is the fourth instance and it is
the one with a gate downstream of it.
